coverage.main: Read all twenty pages of arXiv 1907.10823v3 (27 February 2020): Sections 1-6, Algorithm (Figure 2), Tables 1-3, Figures 1-8, references and Appendices A-H (Tables 4-8, Figures 9-16). Footnote 7 states that earlier versions contained results with incorrect normalization; v3 is treated as the corrected record.
coverage.supplement: Appendices A-H are embedded in the arXiv PDF and read. The CVF ICCV 2019 version was not retrieved; given the footnoted correction, CVF and arXiv v3 values must not be mixed.
coverage.excluded_results: Dagger-marked source=target cells (Tables 2, 5, 8 and figure curves for the source) are white-box. Figures 4, 6, 12 (disturbance/angle diagnostics) and 15 (decision-boundary visualization) are not transfer rates.

result_groups.locator: Section 4 (pp. 4-6), Table 2, Table 3, Figures 3, 7, 8; Appendix A (p. 11), Tables 4-5, 8, Figures 9-11, 13, 16
result_groups.population: All CIFAR-10 test images; four author-trained models (ResNet18, SENet18, DenseNet121, GoogLeNet) as sources and targets
result_groups.outcome: target top-1 accuracy after attack (complement is unconditional misclassification)
result_groups.evidence: Appendix A: adversarial examples are generated 'for all images in the test set' and transferability is evaluated by testing accuracies, so target-clean-incorrect inputs and source failures are retained (source white-box accuracies above zero, e.g., ResNet18 MI-FGSM 5.7%). Explicit unconditioned design, not missing reporting.

result_groups.locator: Section 4.4 and Figure 5 (pp. 5-6); Appendix D and Figure 14
result_groups.population: All 50,000 ImageNet validation images; torchvision ResNet18, DenseNet121, SqueezeNet1.0, AlexNet
result_groups.evidence: Section 4.4 and Appendix D test accuracies 'over adversarial examples generated from all 50000 ImageNet test images', explicitly retaining all inputs and source failures.

result_groups.population: 5,000 randomly selected ImageNet validation images; Cadene Inc-v3 source, Inc-v4 and IncRes-v2 targets; epsilon 0.06
result_groups.evidence: The caption states random selection and 'same as experiment in Table 2' but does not restate whether all selected images and all adversarial examples are evaluated; not coded no from protocol analogy.

result_groups.population: 1,600 adversarial examples (50 batches x 32); selection not stated
result_groups.evidence: Subset construction and conditioning are not described.

f1.evidence: Final CIFAR-10 test accuracies are reported separately for all four CIFAR models (94.8%, 94.6%, 95.6%, 94.9%), covering every source and target in that group. Clean accuracies for the ImageNet torchvision and Cadene Inception models are not reported.

f2.locator: Appendix A; Section 4.4; Table 1; Appendix G
f2.evidence: CIFAR-10 and 50k-ImageNet groups explicitly retain all inputs (no); Table 1 and Appendix G populations are unresolved. Not mixed_explicit because no group is yes.

f3.locator: Appendix A; Section 4.4; Table 1; Appendix G
f3.evidence: Two groups explicitly evaluate all adversarial examples (no); two are unresolved.

f4.evidence: One-decimal percentages over 10,000 CIFAR-10 test images or 5,000/50,000 ImageNet images do not yield unique integer numerators; many results are graphical.

f5.locator: Appendix A (p. 11); Table 1 caption; Section 4.4; Appendix D; Appendix F and Figure 16
f5.evidence: CIFAR-10 uses L-infinity epsilon 0.015 for all attacks (DeepFool clipped); Table 1 uses epsilon 0.06. The ImageNet torchvision experiments (Figure 5, Appendix D) state no radius. Appendix F text lists epsilon 0.01-0.025 while Figure 16 panels are labelled 0.02-0.05. Missing radius for one surveyed scope, so unclear.

f6.evidence: The linked official repository provides attack code, all_in_one evaluators that log clean accuracy and accuracy after attack on the same batches, and a Google Drive folder of the four CIFAR-10 checkpoints (config filenames encode 94.77/95.61/94.86/94.59% accuracy, matching the paper). Config epsilon 0.03 applies to inputs normalized to [-1,1], plausibly equal to the paper's 0.015 on [0,1]; the release's C&W wrapper is untargeted while the paper used a randomized targeted C&W. Drive checkpoints not downloaded and nothing executed. Strong recomputation candidate, not yet verified.

artifact_checks.result: Cloned and pinned (13 tracked files, last commit 24 October 2019). all_in_one_cifar10.py iterates the unshuffled CIFAR-10 test loader for num_batches (README example 50 x 32 = 1,600 images), logging fool_rate (prediction change), acc_after_attack and original_acc for each target and batch. README links a Drive checkpoint folder; ImageNet evaluator uses pretrainedmodels. Not executed.
README-linked CIFAR-10 checkpoint folder; not listed or downloaded in this review.

bounds_checks.locator: Section 4 clean accuracies; Appendix A; Table 2
bounds_checks.reason: Clean test accuracy and attacked accuracy are both on the full CIFAR-10 test set for fixed deterministic models, unconditioned, so max(0, attacked error - clean error) is well defined per target. Not extracted in this review: clean accuracies are printed to 0.1% and several transfer cells appear only in figures; extraction and rounding propagation belong to the corpus-wide bounds pass.
No clean accuracies for the torchvision models on the 50,000 images are reported; results are graphical.
No clean baseline on the evaluated subsets and conditioning unresolved.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit. The epsilon reconciliation between release and paper is an inference from the release normalization, to be checked in any recomputation.
No checkpoint download or execution; CIFAR-10 bound extraction deferred to the corpus-wide pass.
